helpful: The provisioned petition text included the Second Circuit summary order as Appendix A, which was the single most important input: the invited-error and forfeiture holdings are the vehicle problem.
The sal-v4 band table with bracketed reached rates matched the context's salience version, so the pooled baseline anchor was straightforward.
CourtListener opinion search confirmed the cited Eleventh Circuit decision and surfaced the Second Circuit's later published FMLA opinion.
gaps: The CourtListener RECAP docket index returns nothing for SCOTUS dockets, so prior cert petitions on the same question (e.g. Lapham v. Walgreen) could not be checked for a call for a response or a CVSG; a corpus-side keyword or QP-topic search over resolved SCOTUS petitions would fill this.
A statpack cut by whether a response was called for would sharpen the relist-increment claim, which here is almost entirely the CFR hazard.
fedcourts query has no subject filter usable for SCOTUS rows, so the priors query gave docket shape only.
notes: Eleven of twelve MCP calls were cheap; the one opinion-body fetch (Haran) returned the full text and was the only expensive call. Kept to 12 retrieval calls plus one corpus query.
